overview:
A week is the ideal first trip to Morocco, and this itinerary uses it well. You start with a guided day in Marrakech, walk among Berber villages in the High Atlas, cross the mountains by the Tichka pass to the kasbahs and gorges of the south, and then do what most 7-day tours do not: spend two nights in the Sahara. The trip ends in Fes, the great medieval medina, with a full guided day before you fly home or continue north.

Most one-week desert tours give you a single night in the dunes: you arrive tired at sunset and leave at dawn. Here the second desert day is free of long drives – sunrise on the dunes, a 4x4 tour to a nomad family and the Gnawa musicians of Khamlia, and time to rest before a second sunset. Very few operators combine that with a day walking in the Atlas, so you see Morocco's mountains, desert and two imperial cities in one coherent route from south to north.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 7 days, 6 nights
• Start: Marrakech – Finish: Fes
• Nights: Marrakech (2), Dades valley, Merzouga (2 – one in a desert camp), Fes
• Type: private tour with driver; licensed guides in Marrakech and Fes; mountain guide in the Atlas; local guide at Ait Ben Haddou
• Longest drives: Day 3 (about 8 hours with stops) and Day 6 (about 8–9 hours with stops)
• Activity level: easy to moderate; a 3-hour village walk and a 1-hour camel ride
• Meals: breakfast daily; dinner on the three nights in the south

THE ROUTE
Day 1 – Guided day in Marrakech: Koutoubia, Bahia Palace, Ben Youssef madrasa, souks, Majorelle Garden.
Day 2 – High Atlas: Imlil and a walk to the Berber village of Aroumd.
Day 3 – Tichka pass, Ait Ben Haddou, Skoura and the Dades valley.
Day 4 – Todra Gorge, Erfoud and a sunset camel trek to a camp in the Erg Chebbi.
Day 5 – A full day in the Sahara: sunrise, nomad family, Khamlia, free time.
Day 6 – Ziz valley, Midelt, cedar forests and Ifrane to Fes.
Day 7 – Guided day in Fes el-Bali: madrasas, souks, Qarawiyyin and the tannery.

WHY THIS ROUTE WORKS
• Two Sahara nights, so you experience the desert instead of passing through it.
• A real day in the mountains, not just a view from the car.
• A one-way route south to north, so you never drive the same road twice.
• Guided days in both Marrakech and Fes to make sense of the two great medinas.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
First-time visitors with one week, couples, families with children who like the outdoors, photographers and travellers flying into Marrakech and out of Fes.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
With more time, see the [Morocco itinerary 9 days to Tangier](/en-US/morocco/marrakech/tours/morocco-itinerary-9-days-from-marrakech-to-tangier-via-the-sahara-fes-and-chefchaouen/1dc582876c31387bc26b818b). For a slower pace with more nights in the south, the [10-day tour from Marrakech to Fes](/en-US/morocco/marrakech/tours/10-day-morocco-tour-from-marrakech-to-fes-sahara-kasbahs-atlas-mountains/59f7ea95444e8387960d1e5c) adds more stops.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Pack layers: Marrakech can be warm while the Atlas and the desert are cold at night, especially from November to March. Bring walking shoes for Imlil and the medinas, a scarf and sunglasses for the dunes, and a small bag for the camp night. Majorelle tickets are sold online for timed slots; we book them when you confirm.
descriptions:
What to expect: Marrakech with a licensed guide – the medina's monuments in the morning, the souks at midday and the Majorelle Garden in the afternoon.

Your guide meets you at your riad and starts at the Koutoubia, the 12th-century minaret that has dominated Marrakech for 800 years. You walk to the Bahia Palace, a 19th-century vizier's residence of marble courtyards and painted cedar ceilings, then north through the old city to the Ben Youssef madrasa, a Koranic school rebuilt in the 16th century around one of the most beautiful courtyards in Morocco. At midday you explore the souks – the dyers with skeins of wool drying overhead, the spice sellers, the metalworkers and lantern makers – with shopping always optional. After lunch, your driver takes you to the Majorelle Garden, the cobalt-blue garden of cacti and bamboo saved by Yves Saint Laurent. The evening is free for Jemaa el-Fna.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Koutoubia.
09:45 – Bahia Palace (about 1 hour).
11:00 – Ben Youssef madrasa (about 45 min).
12:00 – Dyers' and spice souks.
13:30 – Lunch (not included).
15:00 – Majorelle Garden (timed ticket, about 1 hour).

GOOD TO KNOW
• You walk about 6–8 km on uneven lanes.
• Your guide adjusts the order to avoid crowds.

INCLUDED: licensed guide and driver, riad night with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: entrance fees, lunch, tips.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: the red city with someone who knows it.

Overnight: riad in Marrakech.
Meals: breakfast.

What to expect: a day in the High Atlas – the drive to Imlil and a guided walk through Berber villages and orchards below Jebel Toubkal, with lunch in a village house.

You leave Marrakech across the Haouz plain and climb through the Moulay Brahim gorge and the Asni valley to Imlil, at 1,740 m the starting point for walks around Jebel Toubkal (4,167 m), the highest peak in North Africa. With a mountain guide born in the valley you follow mule paths through walnut and cherry orchards and irrigated terraces to Aroumd, an earth-and-stone village on a rocky spur at about 1,900 m. Your guide explains the irrigation channels, the shared threshing floors and how families live with the seasons. Lunch is a tagine with bread and mint tea on a terrace facing the peaks. In the afternoon you walk back by another path and return to Marrakech.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:30 – Depart Marrakech.
10:00 – Arrive in Imlil.
10:30 – Walk to Aroumd (about 2 hours).
13:00 – Lunch in a village house (not included).
14:00 – Walk back to Imlil.
17:30 – Back at your riad.

GOOD TO KNOW
• About 8 km and 300 m of ascent; it can be shortened, and a mule can be hired.
• It is 10–15°C cooler than Marrakech; snow is possible from December to March.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, mountain guide, riad with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, mule, tips.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: mountain air and a glimpse of Berber village life.

Overnight: riad in Marrakech.
Meals: breakfast.

What to expect: over the High Atlas by the Tichka pass, a guided visit of the UNESCO ksar of Ait Ben Haddou, and the road of a thousand kasbahs to the Dades valley.

You leave early and climb through Berber villages to the Tizi n'Tichka at 2,260 m, the highest main road pass in Morocco. On the southern side the landscape turns red and dry. At Ait Ben Haddou, a fortified village of earthen houses listed by UNESCO in 1987 and used in films from Lawrence of Arabia to Gladiator, a local guide walks you up to the hilltop granary. After lunch you pass Ouarzazate and follow a line of oases east: Skoura with its palm grove and kasbahs, Kelaat M'Gouna in the valley of roses, and finally the Dades valley, where red cliffs and rock formations rise above fig and almond trees.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
07:30 – Pick-up in Marrakech.
10:00 – Tizi n'Tichka (2,260 m).
11:30 – Ait Ben Haddou with a local guide (about 1.5 hours).
13:00 – Lunch (not included).
15:00 – Ouarzazate and Skoura.
16:30 – Valley of Roses.
18:00 – Dades valley; dinner at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• About 330 km and 8 hours with stops; the Tichka road is winding.
• The pass is often cold and windy.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, local guide at Ait Ben Haddou, hotel with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: mountains and kasbahs in one unforgettable road day.

Overnight: hotel in the Dades valley.
Meals: breakfast, dinner.

What to expect: the Todra Gorge in the morning, the oases of the Tafilalet, and a camel trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes for sunset and a night in camp.

You drive east to Tinghir and into the Todra Gorge, where limestone walls about 300 m high close in to 10 m above a clear stream; you walk through the narrowest section. The road then crosses the desert plains past Tinejdad and its khettara water channels to Erfoud, known for its 350-million-year-old fossils. In the late afternoon you reach Merzouga at the foot of the Erg Chebbi, whose dunes rise up to about 150 m. You leave your main luggage and ride a camel into the sand as the light turns gold. Dinner is in camp, followed by drums around the fire and a sky full of stars.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:30 – Depart the Dades.
10:00 – Todra Gorge (about 1 hour).
12:30 – Lunch (not included).
14:30 – Erfoud.
16:30 – Camel trek into the dunes (about 1 hour).
18:30 – Desert camp.

GOOD TO KNOW
• About 280 km and 6–7 hours with stops.
• Bring a small bag and a warm layer for the camp.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, camel trek, desert camp with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: canyons and the Sahara on the same day.

Overnight: desert camp in the Erg Chebbi.
Meals: breakfast, dinner.

What to expect: a full day in the desert without long drives – sunrise on the dunes, a 4x4 tour to a nomad family and the Gnawa village of Khamlia, and free time.

Wake before dawn to climb a dune and watch the sun rise over the Sahara, then have breakfast in camp. Your driver takes you around the Erg Chebbi by 4x4: tea in the goat-hair tent of a nomad family, the village of Khamlia where descendants of West African families play Gnawa music, the seasonal lake of Dayet Srji (with flamingos after wet winters) and old fossil sites on the stony hamada. After lunch in Merzouga you have time to rest, try sandboarding or walk in the dunes before a second sunset. The night is in a camp or a hotel at the foot of the dunes, depending on your package.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
06:00 – Sunrise from the dunes.
08:00 – Breakfast.
09:30 – 4x4 tour: nomad family, Khamlia, fossils (about 3.5 hours).
13:00 – Lunch in Merzouga (not included).
15:00 – Free time; sandboarding optional.
18:00 – Sunset on the dunes; dinner.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Musicians in Khamlia expect a small contribution.
• Ask before photographing nomad families.

INCLUDED: driver and 4x4 tour, accommodation with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: real time in the Sahara, not just a night.

Overnight: Merzouga (camp or hotel by the dunes).
Meals: breakfast, dinner.

What to expect: a last sunrise over the dunes, then north through the Ziz valley, Midelt and the cedar forests of the Middle Atlas to Fes.

After breakfast you leave the desert and drive north through Erfoud and Errachidia into the Ziz gorges, a long palm grove winding through a red canyon, with viewpoints over the oasis. You cross the high plateaus to Midelt, at the foot of the snowy Jebel Ayachi, where you stop for lunch. In the afternoon the road climbs into the Middle Atlas cedar forest near Azrou, where Barbary macaques often wait by the road, and passes Ifrane, an alpine-style town built in the 1930s. You arrive in Fes in the early evening and check into your riad in the medina.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
06:00 – Sunrise.
08:00 – Depart Merzouga.
10:00 – Ziz valley viewpoint (about 15 min).
13:00 – Lunch in Midelt (not included).
15:00 – Cedar forest and macaques.
15:45 – Ifrane (about 20 min).
17:30 – Arrival in Fes.

GOOD TO KNOW
• About 470 km and 8–9 hours with stops – the longest day.
• Please do not feed the macaques.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, riad with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: from the dunes to the cedars in a single day.

Overnight: riad in Fes.
Meals: breakfast.

What to expect: a full day in Fes el-Bali with a licensed guide – madrasas, souks, the Qarawiyyin and the Chouara tannery.

Your guide starts at the golden gates of the Royal Palace and the Mellah, the old Jewish quarter, then enters the medina at Bab Bou Jeloud, the blue gate. Inside is a labyrinth of more than 9,000 lanes where donkeys still carry goods. You see the Bou Inania madrasa, a 14th-century school of carved cedar and zellige, walk down the Talaa Kebira through the souks, and see from outside the Qarawiyyin, founded in 859 and often called the oldest university in the world, and the Attarine madrasa. The day ends at the Chouara tannery, where hides are dyed in stone vats as they have been for centuries. The tour ends at your riad; we can arrange your transfer to Fes airport or the train station.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Royal Palace gates and the Mellah.
10:00 – Bab Bou Jeloud and Bou Inania.
11:30 – The souks.
13:00 – Lunch (not included).
14:30 – Qarawiyyin and Attarine madrasa.
15:30 – Chouara tannery.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Workshop visits are optional; buying is never required.
• If your flight leaves on Day 7, we can shorten the visit or add a night.

INCLUDED: licensed guide, riad with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: entrance fees, lunch, tips.

WHAT YOU'LL TASTE
Pastilla, bissara bean soup and honey pastries.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: the world's largest living medieval city, at the end of a week that covered mountains, desert and two imperial capitals.

Meals: breakfast.

faq.question: Is a week enough?
faq.answer: Yes, for a great first trip. In seven days you see Marrakech, the High Atlas, the kasbahs and gorges of the south, two nights in the Sahara and Fes. You will not see the north or the coast; for that, choose a longer itinerary.

faq.question: Is it private?
faq.answer: Yes. The vehicle, driver and guides are only for your group, so you set the pace and can change stops along the way.

faq.question: Which meals are included?
faq.answer: Breakfast every day and dinner on the three nights in the south (Dades, desert camp and Merzouga). Lunches and city dinners are not included.

faq.question: Why two nights in the desert?
faq.answer: With one night you arrive at sunset and leave at dawn. The second night gives you a full day for sunrise, a 4x4 tour, a nomad family and Gnawa music, with time to rest – it is the part travellers remember most.

faq.question: How hard is the Atlas walk?
faq.answer: Easy to moderate: about 8 km and 300 m of ascent over 3–4 hours on village paths. It can be shortened, and a mule can carry anyone who prefers not to walk uphill.

faq.question: How much driving is there?
faq.answer: Days 3 and 6 are long (about 8–9 hours with stops) and Day 4 about 6–7 hours. Days 1, 5 and 7 have very little driving.

faq.question: What is the desert camp like?
faq.answer: Berber-style tents in the dunes with beds, blankets and toilets. Luxury camps with en-suite bathrooms are available depending on the package.

faq.question: Can the tour end in Marrakech instead of Fes?
faq.answer: Yes, but returning from Merzouga to Marrakech is a long day. We can also reverse the route, starting in Fes and ending in Marrakech.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, for children who enjoy walking and road trips. The camels, dunes, macaques and the village walk are usually highlights. Child seats are available.

faq.question: When is the best time to go?
faq.answer: March to May and September to November are ideal. Summer is very hot in the desert, and winter nights are cold in the Atlas and Sahara, but the trip runs all year.

faq.question: What should I pack?
faq.answer: Layers, walking shoes, a scarf and sunglasses for the dunes, sunscreen, a small overnight bag for the camp and covering clothes for the cities and mosques.

faq.question: Do we need to book Majorelle in advance?
faq.answer: Yes. Tickets are sold online for timed slots and often sell out. We book them for Day 1 once you confirm.

faq.question: Can I add Chefchaouen?
faq.answer: Yes. Add a day or two after Fes to visit Chefchaouen, or choose our 9-day itinerary to Tangier, which includes the blue town.
